why_relevant: 2,000 m2 expo with 30+ exhibitors — a near-complete vendor census for regional payments at a point in time. Fetched directly: the page is promotional and does NOT name exhibitors, so the exhibitor roster must be recovered from the event app, floorplan or press coverage.

source_name: PayTech.Events / European Digital Finance Association event listings
why_relevant: Third-party aggregators of payments-industry events with dates, agendas and links; useful for discovering regional payments events (beyond Money Motion) that Slovenian vendors and banks attend, and for backfilling past editions.

Slovenia's largest information-security conference (24th edition, Nova Gorica, Sept 2026) with an explicit sponsor tier and exhibitor list — observed names include Cloudflare (general sponsor), ADD, CreaPlus, Delinea, Kaspersky, Kontron, Omicron, Sophos. Banks are a core buyer segment for these vendors; security-vendor visibility spend maps directly onto bank fraud/cyber procurement.

source_name: iVarnost.si – event reporting and award coverage
why_relevant: Slovenian security-media outlet that files post-event reports naming award recipients, sponsors and attendance figures; recovers detail that conference sites delete after the edition ends.

source_name: Računalniške novice – IT event calendar (koledar dogodkov)
why_relevant: The most complete Slovenian IT-event calendar, with per-event pages for DSI, INFOSEK, CIO Summit, NT konferenca, Industrijski forum IRT. Best single pointer for discovering Slovenian conferences where banking/payments vendors buy visibility, and for dates/venues.

Long-running Slovenian Microsoft-ecosystem/enterprise-IT conference (Grand Hotel Bernardin, Portorož, Sept 2026) with a partner/sponsor exhibition; Slovenian system integrators serving banks routinely exhibit there.

Executive-level IT-buyer summit (Ljubljana, Feb 2026, cybersecurity focus). CIO-level audiences are exactly the bank decision-makers vendors pay to reach; the sponsor list is a short, high-intent vendor set.

38th+ edition academic-industry e-business conference run by the eCenter of the University of Maribor. Its Business Track hosts panels/workshops with industry, and its Research Track publishes payments-relevant papers (e.g. digital payment methods, cashless payment ecosystems). Long-run archive makes it a stable index of who frames Slovenian digital-payments discourse.

CEE/Adriatic startup-investor conference (11-13 May 2026) with an explicit fintech track, 220 selected startups and 60+ VC funds; co-organised with the Slovene Enterprise Fund and the Ministry of Economy. Best source for emerging Slovenian/regional fintech challengers and for corporate-partner (bank) sponsorship of startup programmes.

source_name: DIGGIT awards – winners archive (financial services / insurance / banking category)
why_relevant: Slovenian digital-project awards with an explicit financial services, insurance and banking category. 2025 winners in that category: Zavarovalnica Triglav ('Ali tveganje živi na vašem naslovu?') and Mastercard Slovenija with agency Povem ('Geste vključenosti / Prispevaj kretnjo'). Entries name client + agency + technology partner, i.e. a disclosed vendor-client pairing.

14th edition (2025) awarded 38 prizes across 225 submitted projects; the 2025 overall champion was Mastercard Slovenija with agency Povem. Award entries are self-declared vendor-client case studies covering banking/payments digital projects.

Long-running .si web-project award with category winners including corporate and financial-sector sites; each winning entry names the commissioning organisation and the agency/technology supplier, giving disclosed digital-vendor relationships for Slovenian banks and insurers.

source_name: GZS Priznanja za inovacije / Dan inovativnosti (innovation awards)
why_relevant: The largest and most prestigious Slovenian innovation award system (24th national call; 245 proposals, 10 gold / 27 silver / 15 bronze in the latest cycle), run by GZS and 13 regional chambers. Applications describe product/process/marketing/organisational innovations with named innovator teams and companies — a screening ground for fintech/payments innovations and their corporate sponsors.

source_name: Dnevi zavarovalništva v Sloveniji (Slovenian Insurance Days) – Slovensko zavarovalno združenje
why_relevant: The central Slovenian insurance-sector event (30th edition 2024, GH Bernardin Portorož, 400+ participants). Bancassurance, payments and core-system vendors court insurers here; the insurer-side vendor set overlaps heavily with banking. Relevant because run scope is sector=both.

The business daily Finance runs a large commercial conference portfolio (incl. Finančna konferenca, Portorož) sold with sponsorship packages. Sponsor and speaker rosters here are paid declarations by vendors targeting Slovenian CFOs, treasurers and bank staff.

Global event aggregator with per-event exhibitor/visitor counts and organiser links; useful as a cross-check and discovery layer for Slovenian and Adriatic banking/payments/IT events not covered by local calendars.

source_name: SBC – Klub slovenskih podjetnikov (Slovenian Business Club)
why_relevant: 450-member entrepreneurs' club running conferences, press conferences and webinars; its member directory and event partners identify Slovenian companies (incl. IT/fintech suppliers) and the banks that sponsor business-community events. Weaker signal than dedicated banking events but useful for partnership mapping.

source_name: ASEE newsroom – regional payments event coverage
why_relevant: ASEE (with Monri) co-founded Money Motion and publishes named post-event recaps listing co-sponsors (Nexi, Mastercard, OTP Bank, Payten). A direct competitor's own visibility record, dated and self-declared — the highest-signal form of sponsorship evidence.

source_name: Finance.si (Casnik Finance) - business daily, gospodarstvo/IKT desks
why_relevant: Slovenia's only business daily; the single most likely outlet to name contract values, displaced incumbents and tender disputes in bank IT/payments supplier deals. Publishes vendor-deal news, bank management interviews and annual IT/IKT supplement content.

Consumer-finance monthly from the Finance publishing house; covers retail bank product launches, mobile/e-banking rollouts and fee changes, which indirectly reveal which vendor platform a bank has adopted.

National daily of record; covers bank mergers (SKB/Nova KBM into OTP), service outages during migrations, and Bank of Slovenia fee comparisons. Migration-outage stories are a reliable tell for core-system/vendor changes.

source_name: Dnevnik - gospodarstvo / Zlata nit awards coverage
why_relevant: Second national daily; its Zlata nit employer awards and business pages regularly profile Slovenian IT suppliers to banks (e.g. Halcom), yielding company-level context, headcount and project narratives rarely published elsewhere.

National news agency; the origin wire for most Slovenian bank/vendor announcements later reprinted by Delo, Zurnal24, 24ur and RTVSLO. Also runs an English service, making it a bilingual anchor for A6 press monitoring.

Highest-volume Slovenian IT trade outlet with an explicit business-solutions/digitalisation vertical. Confirmed to carry vendor-named banking project write-ups (Comtrade Digital Services at Hypo, Halcom regulated-sector work, SRC regional bank deployments, NLB digital programmes) - effectively free vendor case studies.

Slovenia's long-running IT magazine; confirmed article on back-office banking digitalisation and on Slovenian IT firms abroad. Independent lab-test culture gives it more editorial distance from vendors than pure trade portals.

source_name: Monitor Pro (B2B enterprise-IT edition of Monitor)
why_relevant: The enterprise/CIO-facing sister title; PDF back-issues are published on monitor.si and carry supplier interviews, project retrospectives and integrator profiles - exactly the mid-size supplier stories missing from English sources.

Highest-value single find for this cell: document-based investigative reporting on a failed BKS Bank core-system migration (duplicated standing orders, wrong statements, foreign-language output). This is precisely the internal-friction and implementation-failure detail neither bank nor vendor publishes.
